prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map orders the indoor room from the camera wearer's held banknotes at the bottom edge (~0.3 m, brightest white) and the white coat draped over a chair directly in front (~0.4–0.6 m, within the camera wearer's arm's reach) to a standing person behind and slightly left of the coat (~0.8–1.2 m from the camera wearer and ~0.3–0.5 m behind the coat), with a recessed window on the left and a white shelf unit, small shelf items, and a dustpan/broom against the right wall (~1.8–2.5 m away, ~1.2–1.5 m behind and right of the coat). Across frames 1 to 4, the coat remains in the near foreground occluding the standing person's right torso while the person's hands reach above the coat collar within arm's reach in frames 2 and 4 (~0.6–0.8 m), and in frame 5 the viewpoint shifts upward past the coat to show the person's torso and both forearms facing the camera wearer at ~0.8–1.0 m alongside the shelf unit on the right (~1.2–1.8 m). In all five frames, the standing person's head is cropped above the top edge of the view so whether their eyes look toward the camera wearer cannot be confirmed, while the banknotes and lower chair remain partly cropped at the bottom. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the white coat from the similarly coloured white wall and shelf behind it and shows the continuous recessed plane of the floor and walls. However, the depth map is unreliable across the glass window (rendering outdoor trees as uniformly black/infinite depth in frame 5 while flattening the window sill in frames 1–4) and loses fine depth boundaries on the thin wire chair legs and between the overlapping coat and banknotes.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map labels two overlapping foreground regions in frames 1–4: a pink 'person' mask on the white coat in the centre (~0.4–0.6 m away, within the camera wearer's arm's reach) and a second brown or green 'person' mask on the standing person behind and to the left (~0.8–1.2 m away, ~0.3–0.5 m behind the coat, facing the camera wearer with their head cropped at the top edge and right side occluded by the coat). To the right of and ~1.2–1.5 m behind the coat (~1.8–2.5 m from the camera wearer), the map intermittently segments the lower shelf cube as a purple or green 'chair' in frames 2–4 and the orange object above it as a 'book' in frame 2, while leaving the room walls, window, broom, and foreground banknotes (~0.3 m below) unsegmented black. Across frames 1 to 4, the standing person's mask shrinks on the left as the coat shifts slightly left to occlude more of their body, and in frame 5, once the coat drops out of view, a single pink 'person' mask covers the standing person's upper body and arms facing the camera wearer at ~0.8–1.0 m (within arm's reach of the foreground banknotes). Beyond RGB, the masks explicitly delineate the boundary where the standing person's hands and torso emerge behind the coat in frames 1–3. However, the segmentation map is highly unreliable in class assignment and completeness: it misclassifies the coat on a chair as a 'person' in frames 1–4, mislabels the right-hand shelf as a 'chair', misses the standing person's left arm in frame 4, and leaves the foreground cash and background walls completely unlabelled.
descriptions.pose: The skeleton map is completely blank in frames 1, 3, and 4 because the white coat in the foreground (~0.4–0.6 m away) occludes the standing person's body (~0.8–1.2 m away, ~0.3–0.5 m behind the coat) and the person's head is cropped above the top frame edge throughout the sequence. In frame 2, a single magenta hand skeleton appears near the top centre at ~0.7 m where the standing person's left hand reaches above the coat collar within arm's reach of the coat and the camera wearer. In frame 5, after the coat moves below the field of view, a yellow torso-and-arm skeleton with two magenta hand skeletons appears directly in front of the camera wearer at ~0.8–1.0 m, showing the person facing the camera wearer with elbows bent and both hands held forward at waist level (~0.6–0.8 m, within arm's reach of both the person and the camera wearer's foreground banknotes at ~0.3–0.5 m). Compared to the RGB image, the frame 5 skeleton makes the 3D articulation of the person's shoulders, elbows, wrists, and curled fingers explicit despite motion blur and dark clothing. However, the pose map is unreliable across the sequence: it misses the visible right hand and left-side body in frame 2, detects no keypoints at all in frames 1, 3, and 4, misses the camera wearer's own hand holding cash at the bottom of frame 5, and places noisy torso and hip lines near the bottom of frame 5 where the lower body is cropped out of view.
